classification.difficultyReason: Complete a two-dice sample-space array and count outcomes satisfying several events, including an inclusive or.

inlines.text: Rows: Die 1 = 1–6. Columns: Die 2 = 1–6. Each pair is (Die 2, Die 1).

answer.worked: In each cell, write (Die 2 result, Die 1 result): the column number first and the row number second. Across each row the first number runs from 1 to 6; down each column the second number runs from 1 to 6.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the total number of outcomes?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the probability that the outcome is:

answer.worked:
Only one of the 36 equally likely cells is $(1,1)$.
$$P((1,1))=\frac{1}{36}$$

The six diagonal cells have matching numbers, from $(1,1)$ to $(6,6)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{same number})&=\frac{6}{36}\\&=\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}$$

The rows for 1 and 6 contain 12 cells. In each of the other four rows, two cells contain a 1 or 6.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Favourable outcomes}&=12+4\times2\\&=20\\P(\text{1 or 6})&=\frac{20}{36}\\&=\frac{5}{9}\end{aligned}$$
